subject: general
question: What is the Forty-Second Amendment of the Indian Constitution commonly known as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mini-Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Forty-Second Amendment of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1976**, is commonly referred to as the **Mini-Constitution** due to its extensive and comprehensive nature.
 
• It was introduced during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** and is one of the most far-reaching amendments in the history of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The amendment affected **59 Articles** and added **14 new Articles**, significantly altering the Constitution's structure.
 
• It introduced the terms **"Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity"** in the Preamble, emphasizing the core values of the Indian state.
 
• The amendment also curtailed the power of the judiciary, strengthened the authority of Parliament, and redefined the relationship between the Executive and Judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emergency Period:** The amendment was passed during the Emergency (1975–1977), a period characterized by significant centralization of power and suppression of dissent.
 
• **Directive Principles:** It gave primacy to the Directive Principles of State Policy over Fundamental Rights, emphasizing the welfare state model.
 
• **Tenure of Lok Sabha and State Assemblies:** The amendment extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from **5 to 6 years**.
 
• **Judicial Review:** It restricted the judiciary's ability to challenge constitutional amendments and curtailed its power to review laws passed by Parliament.
 
• **Criticism:** The Forty-Second Amendment faced widespread criticism for its authoritarian nature, and many of its provisions were later repealed or modified by the **Forty-Fourth Amendment Act (1978)**.
